chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Amr ibn Saeed al-Madaini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the man who forgets a letter from the Quran and remembers it while he is bowing (ruku'), is it permissible for him to recite during the bowing? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but when he prostrates (sajdah), let him recite.'

key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: One who is bowing in prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they forget a Quranic letter while bowing in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the precise moment for completing Quranic recitation during prayer, distinguishing between the state of bowing (ruku') and prostration (sajdah). It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the structural integrity of prayer movements, ensuring that recitation is completed in its proper place rather than extending it into the subsequent posture. This ruling underscores the meticulous attention to detail (dqa'iq) characteristic of Imami fiqh regarding the validity of acts of worship.
